cards.text: Israel is on the move again, traveling along the road to Atharim. Down in the Negev, a king hears they're coming. A whole nation walking down your road is not exactly a quiet visit, friend. Even I would've heard that from the back of my old junk drawer.

cards.question: The king who hears that Israel is coming is the Canaanite king of ___.
When the king of Arad hears Israel is coming along the road to Atharim, he lets them pass by in peace.

cards.text: Nope, no welcome cookies, no wave from the porch. He ATTACKS Israel, and he doesn't leave empty-handed.

cards.question: What does the king of Arad take from Israel when he attacks?

cards.text: So what does Israel do after a hit like that? Me, I'd crawl back into my old junk drawer and hide under the takeout menus, but Israel does something a WHOLE lot better.

cards.question: After the attack from Arad, what does Israel do?

answers.text: They make a vow to the LORD
They build an altar to the LORD

cards.question: In Israel's vow, what do they ask the LORD to do?

answers.text: Hand the people of Arad over to them
Give them a safe road past Arad
Lead them far away from the Negev

cards.text: And if He does, here's Israel's side of the deal: "we will devote their cities to destruction." Friend, the biggest promise I ever make is to stop eating the chocolate chips before they hit the dough, and I can't even keep THAT one.

cards.question: The LORD hears Israel's plea and delivers up the Canaanites.

cards.text: The LORD came through. Now Israel's promise is sitting on the counter, and that timer is going DING, DING, DING.

cards.question: After the LORD delivers up the Canaanites, what does Israel do with the vow they made?

cards.text: Israel devotes the Canaanites and their cities to destruction, just like they said. Then they name the place, and it's a whole lot more serious than the name I gave my first burnt batch.

cards.question: What does Israel name the place where the Canaanites of Arad were defeated?

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences, exceeding the three-sentence limit.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: The king first appears only as "a king." His identifying description as the Canaanite king of Arad is withheld instead of being given when he is introduced.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blank asks for Arad even though no earlier card has named Arad or provided a clue to it, leaving the baker to guess an unseen place name.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
